failure_summary.description: Agents returned a salient associated item or placeholder rather than the target requested by the clue, despite existing target and wordplay guidance.
The underlying answers were identifiable, but title spacing and a name spelling differed from the expected forms.
A bare person-name prompt lacked guidance for inferring a clearly foregrounded contextual relation rather than returning the person's office.
Advice to omit implicit type words led to shortening a conventional geographic name.

patch.reasoning: Most target-selection misses are already covered by the skill's slot, relation, and wordplay rules, so repeating them would not address the gap. The edits clarify when a type word belongs to a conventional name and add a cautious rule for bare person-name prompts. The spelling and title-variant mismatches are already covered by existing form guidance and do not warrant duplicating it.

edits.target: When choosing a name form, distinguish identity-bearing parts from generic type words supplied by the clue. Retain conventional initials that belong to a person's identifying name; omit a generic label such as an entity type or location type when the clue supplies that type and the shorter name identifies the answer unambiguously.
edits.content: When choosing a name form, distinguish genuinely generic labels from words that form part of the entity's conventional proper name. Retain conventional initials and lexicalized type words in established names; omit an entity or location type label only if it is not part of the conventional name and the shorter form is accepted and unambiguous.

For a prompt consisting only of a person's name, infer an omitted relation from context only when one relation is clearly foregrounded—for example, when context consistently identifies an officeholder with a particular jurisdiction. Answer that relation rather than merely repeating the person's title or office. If several relations are equally plausible, do not guess.
